evidence.note: Built HTTP smoke-test script, IRC gateway test, and WebSocket cross-node fanout/resume tests — self-constructed checks spanning multiple transports the grader won't hand over.
Actively simulated both resilience scenarios: SIGKILL one HTTP node with restart, and killed the broadcaster to confirm continued cross-node fan-out — the core adversarial probes.
Playwright browser pass against the SPA found issues, drove index.html edits (91-92), then re-tested (95-97) — failures used to drive fixes and re-verify, hitting the pinned semantic elements.
Tested restart timing after kill (node-restart-within-60s window), WS resume+gap semantics, log inspection for errors, and static served from all 3 nodes — mirroring grader invariants.
Exercised slash commands, invitations, files, mentions, read-state, DMs, roles, pins, groups, short-password 400, and IRC↔web bridging into shared seq — broad error-code and cross-protocol coverage.
Cold-boot from clean state as a final end-to-end re-verification rather than trusting prior passes.

reasoning: The agent self-built checks spanning all four transports (HTTP codes/envelopes, WS subscribe/resume/gap/seq, IRC join/privmsg/bridging, Playwright SPA against pinned testids) and actively injected both required failures — killing an HTTP node (with restart-timing verification) and the broadcaster — which fully satisfies the [8] anchor. It also reaches into [10] behavior: browser pass against pinned elements, failures found (SPA) driving fixes and re-verification, and a cold-boot end-to-end re-check. It stops just short of a fully unified repeatable harness and explicit exactly-once fan-out assertions, placing it at 9.
